A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same noise-curriculum SSL framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST experiments, ImageNet classification results, Oxford/Paris retrieval evaluations, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds denoiser-quality experiments, clean-pretrained and mixed-data baseline evaluations, and PCA feature visualizations.

M1.justification: The denoised-to-noisy curriculum, training restart, frozen denoised teacher, regularization loss, and denoiser-free downstream procedure remain unchanged. The additional baseline and ablation configurations do not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: The represented datasets, tasks, corruption types, and noise levels remain unchanged. New tests use existing ImageNet coverage. LVD-142M is identified as the training source of released comparator checkpoints, rather than a newly processed training or evaluation dataset.

E2.justification: Appendix C adds clean-pretrained DINOv2 comparators, including official ViT-B/14 and ViT-S/14 checkpoints, and a baseline trained on randomly mixed noisy and denoised images. These supplement the retained noisy-only, denoiser-preprocessed, and other SSL comparisons.

E3.justification: New supplementary experiments vary denoiser training across 1, 5, and 100 epochs, evaluate frozen clean-pretrained backbones with clean-trained or noisy-trained probes, and test 50/50 noisy-denoised training. Existing experiment settings remain unchanged. The fixed-noise-generation statement is additional disclosure, not evidence of a revised protocol.

E4.justification: The appendix substantially expands checks of the framework's assumptions: B.6 tests sensitivity to denoiser quality; C.1 examines clean-pretrained models under noise; C.2 tests random mixing as an alternative to staging; and D.3 adds dense-feature PCA case studies. Earlier component, initialization, scheduling, and mixed-clean-data analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 17-run MNIST experiment, one-sigma summaries, and Figure 6 box plots. The new experiments add no run-count disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: New results establish additional findings: Table 9 reports NC accuracies of 66.1, 67.4, and 68.1 for 1-, 5-, and 100-epoch denoisers; Table 10 reports clean-pretrained models' noise sensitivity; Table 11 reports 48.0 for mixed training versus 55.4 for noisy-only training. Figure 23 adds qualitative feature results. Table 2 changes NCT scores from 71.5/54.9 to 72.1/55.8, matching values already present in v1 Table 1b. Section 4.1 also corrects SNR summaries, without establishing changed noise settings.

T1.justification: The curriculum definitions, entropy conditions, objectives, and noise-generation equations are retained. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and headline 4.8-point ImageNet-1k improvement. The additional experiments support the existing noise-aware, denoiser-free learning claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 now grounds the denoiser-dependence discussion in the one-epoch ablation. New appendix interpretations argue that weak denoisers can suffice, random mixing harms representation alignment, and PCA patterns indicate stronger semantic features. The synthetic-noise and curriculum-tuning limitations remain; the broad denoiser-tolerance interpretation exceeds the single tested noise setting.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies that noisy datasets are generated once before training rather than corrupted during loading. Added sections document denoiser budgets, pretrained checkpoint configurations, probe conditions, and PCA visualization procedures. Existing implementation details, hardware information, and code-access statement remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Guo et al.'s 2025 SAR ship-detection paper as reference 17 in the remote-sensing motivation. The remaining literature and substantive novelty positioning are retained; most citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely preserved, with localized additions and a revised limitations passage. The appendix gains B.6 and a baseline-comparison section; existing visualizations move from C to D. Cross-references, the appendix outline, and the conference footer are updated.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9–11 and the PCA montage in Figure 23. Existing graphical content is retained, while Figure 7, Figure 13, and noisy-image examples are relocated or redistributed. These are localized display additions and layout changes rather than a broad redesign.

improvement.justification: The new denoiser-quality and alternative-baseline studies address practical questions left untested in v1, while fixed-noise disclosure and corrected Table 2 values improve reproducibility and consistency. The gain is limited: the core evidence remains unchanged, new studies stay within synthetic-noise settings and add no uncertainty estimates, and some denoiser-tolerance interpretations are broader than the demonstrated evidence.
